bibl.title: Noninvasive optical inhibition with a red-shifted microbial rhodopsin

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how to silence neurons over large volumes and at depth without putting anything into the brain
span.quote: A major limit to the utility of optogenetic inhibition is the addressable quantity of neural tissue. Previous optogenetic hyperpolarizing proton pumps (Arch 1 , ArchT 3 , Mac 1 ) and chloride pumps (eNpHR 4 , eNpHR3.0 (ref. 2 )) have successfully inhibited volumes of approximately a cubic millimeter, but many neuroscience questions require the ability to suppress larger tissue volumes.

span.label: whether a red-shifted chloride pump can be engineered to give enough photocurrent for inhibition through intact skull
span.quote: Because red light is less absorbed by hemoglobin than blue, green or yellow wavelengths, we reasoned this red-light sensitivity might render deep brain regions more accessible. We validated this through Monte Carlo modeling and direct measurement in the live mouse brain

span.label: Jaws, a cruxhalorhodopsin with the most red-shifted spectrum of any inhibitor, giving roughly threefold photocurrents at red wavelengths and enabling transcranial silencing 1-3 mm deep in awake mice
span.quote: Optogenetic inhibition of the electrical activity of neurons enables the causal assessment of their contributions to brain functions. Red light penetrates deeper into tissue than other visible wavelengths. We present a red-shifted cruxhalorhodopsin, Jaws, derived from Haloarcula ( Halobacterium ) salinarum (strain Shark) and engineered to result in red light–induced photocurrents three times those of earlier silencers.

span.label: method
span.quote: We present a red-shifted cruxhalorhodopsin, Jaws, derived from Haloarcula ( Halobacterium ) salinarum (strain Shark) and engineered to result in red light–induced photocurrents three times those of earlier silencers.

span.label: optogenetic neural inhibition
span.quote: Optogenetic inhibition of the electrical activity of neurons enables the causal assessment of their contributions to brain functions.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: To enable noninvasive large-volume optogenetic inhibition, we engineered and characterized Jaws, a spectrally shifted cruxhalorhodopsin derived from the species H. salinarum (strain Shark) 17 , which mediates strong red light–driven neural inhibition.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Haemoglobin absorbs red light less than shorter wavelengths, so red-shifting the opsin's action spectrum lets usable light reach deeper brain tissue, which is what makes large-volume and transcranial inhibition possible.
span.quote: Because red light is less absorbed by hemoglobin than blue, green or yellow wavelengths, we reasoned this red-light sensitivity might render deep brain regions more accessible.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A minority of recorded neurons increase firing under illumination because inhibition of upstream neurons removes their drive (network disinhibition), not because the opsin excites them.
span.quote: As others have reported, we observed a small number of neurons across multiple in vivo experiments that increased firing during optical illumination delivered either transcranially or from a 200-µm fiber, most likely as a result of network inhibition from upstream neurons

span.label: red light reaches deeper because hemoglobin, myoglobin and lipid absorb it less than blue or yellow
span.quote: It has been previously well established that optical penetrance of mammalian tissues in the red to near-infrared (600–1,000 nm) wavelengths is better than that of bluer wavelengths, as a result of substantially less absorption from hemoglobin, myoglobin and lipid.

span.label: the gain came from two point mutations plus trafficking sequences borrowed from a potassium channel
span.quote: We subsequently engineered Halo57 by identifying K200R and W214F point mutations 19 , 20 ( Fig. 1b ), which significantly boosted photocurrents without altering its red action spectrum ( n = 9 or 10 cells; P = 0.02, ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc test), and by appending the KGC 21 or ER2 (ref. 22 ) trafficking sequences from the potassium channel Kir2.1 to result in the final molecules Jaws (KGC + ER2) and Jaws-ER2 (ER2)

span.label: rebound after illumination is attributed variously to hyperpolarisation-activated currents or to chloride accumulation shifting the reversal potential
span.quote: A rebound burst of action potentials is common after illumination of cells expressing halorhodopsins 18 , 27 – 30 or archaerhodopsins 18 , 27 , 31 , which respectively pump chloride inward and protons outward.

span.label: ramping the light down rather than switching it off halves the rebound rate and delays it fourfold
span.quote: We attempted to ameliorate this by gradually ramping down illumination over a duration of 200–1,000 ms and found that the mean rebound instantaneous firing rate dropped significantly, from 52 ± 12 Hz to 23 ± 6 Hz ( n = 16 units; P = 0.0065, paired t -test), suggesting that sculpting of light pulses may enable rebound reduction.

span.label: the few neurons that increased firing are attributed to inhibition of upstream neurons rather than a direct effect
span.quote: As others have reported, we observed a small number of neurons across multiple in vivo experiments that increased firing during optical illumination delivered either transcranially or from a 200-µm fiber, most likely as a result of network inhibition from upstream neurons

span.label: The noninvasive results cannot be shown to be direct rather than mediated by network effects or illumination of superficial apical dendrites.
span.quote: We therefore cannot explicitly rule out the possibility that the observed noninvasive results were the result of indirect network activity or apical dendritic illumination: a caveat for any in vivo investigation of noninvasive optogenetics.

span.label: Transcranial illumination cannot be confined to deep tissue with this setup.
span.quote: It is not possible to noninvasively illuminate only deep volumes with our experimental setup without also targeting surface and intermediate layers.

span.label: Jaws still produces post-illumination rebound spiking, which constrains experimental design.
span.quote: Like all previous inhibitors, Jaws does yield post-illumination rebound, which likely has implications for careful experiment design comparable to those for earlier inhibitors such as eNpHR3.0.

span.label: Experiments were essentially unblinded and unrandomised.
span.quote: No blinding was carried out, with the exception of cotransfected opsin-GFP and tdTomato data sets, as the chief goal of the paper was to demonstrate the capabilities of a new technology.

span.label: the method cannot illuminate deep tissue without also illuminating everything above it, so direct deep inhibition cannot be separated from surface or dendritic effects
span.quote: It is not possible to noninvasively illuminate only deep volumes with our experimental setup without also targeting surface and intermediate layers. We therefore cannot explicitly rule out the possibility that the observed noninvasive results were the result of indirect network activity or apical dendritic illumination: a caveat for any in vivo investigation of noninvasive optogenetics.

span.label: Jaws produces MORE post-illumination rebound than the inhibitors it replaces
span.quote: We similarly observed post-illumination rebound in Jaws-, eNpHR3.0- and ArchT-transduced neurons, and Jaws produced greater effects than eNpHR3.0 or ArchT ( Fig. 3e ; n = 8–32 units; P < 0.05, ANOVA with Newman-Keuls post hoc test).

span.label: myelination still affects light propagation, so red penetrance is not uniform across preparations
span.quote: Despite this better red light penetrance, however, myelination may still affect optical propagation in neural tissue and should therefore be taken into account given the experimental system in question

span.label: the two beneficial mutations do not transfer to the halorhodopsin they were modelled on, so the engineering is scaffold-specific
span.quote: In accord with the low sequence conservation, the two homologous point mutations did not enhance the N. pharaonis halorhodopsin

span.label: even improved, the restored retinal spiking reaches about 190 Hz against a wild-type range of 15-450 Hz
span.quote: However, the resultant spiking rates are limited to less than 200 Hz, substantially less than the full wild-type range of 15–450 Hz (ref. 24 ), and thus potentially limit fine visual perception in future clinical use.

span.label: Monte Carlo simulation of light propagation with Henyey-Greenstein and Gegenbauer-kernel anisotropic scattering phase functions, imported to predict how deep red light penetrates brain tissue and skull
span.quote: To achieve accurate simulations of light propagation close to the optical fiber, before the orientation of photon trajectories is randomized by multiple scattering events, we used an anisotropic scattering model with either Henyey-Greenstein or Gegenbauer kernel phase functions, as indicated below.

span.label: a rhodopsin from a halophilic archaeon, screened as a scaffold rather than studied for itself
span.quote: We therefore screened members of the cruxhalorhodopsin class in primary neuronal culture to identify molecules with both red-shifted action spectra and robust photocurrents ( Fig. 1a and Supplementary Fig. 2 ) and identified a hyperpolarizer we named Halo57, the cruxhalorhodopsin from H. salinarum (strain Shark), with less than 60% homology to the Natronomonas pharaonis halorhodopsin

span.label: trafficking sequences taken from the Kir2.1 potassium channel to improve membrane delivery
span.quote: We subsequently engineered Halo57 by identifying K200R and W214F point mutations 19 , 20 ( Fig. 1b ), which significantly boosted photocurrents without altering its red action spectrum ( n = 9 or 10 cells; P = 0.02, ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc test), and by appending the KGC 21 or ER2 (ref. 22 ) trafficking sequences from the potassium channel Kir2.1 to result in the final molecules Jaws (KGC + ER2) and Jaws-ER2 (ER2)

span.label: Monte Carlo modelling of light transport, used to justify the wavelength choice before any protein was made
span.quote: Because red light is less absorbed by hemoglobin than blue, green or yellow wavelengths, we reasoned this red-light sensitivity might render deep brain regions more accessible. We validated this through Monte Carlo modeling and direct measurement in the live mouse brain

span.label: yellow light at 593 nm, close to the spectral peak of both opsins, used to identify which neurons express the opsin, with paired recordings of the same neurons across wavelengths
span.quote: Yellow light (593 nm) was used as a positive control to identify opsin-expressing neurons, owing to its proximity to both Jaws’s and eNpHR3.0’s spectral peaks, and we conducted paired recordings of individual opsin-expressing neurons to assess their performance under different wavelengths ( Fig. 4f ).

span.label: paired recordings with an acutely inserted 200-um fiber as a positive control against transcranial illumination through the intact skull - marked PARTIAL because the paper reports in its own words that this did not settle the question
span.quote: To directly address the possibility that opsin-expressing apical dendrites near the brain’s surface were being hyperpolarized, resulting in somatic or downstream network inhibition, we next conducted paired recordings using a standard acutely inserted 200-µm fiber as a positive control for transcranial illumination outside the mouse’s intact skull.

span.label: Jaws
span.quote: We similarly observed post-illumination rebound in Jaws-, eNpHR3.0- and ArchT-transduced neurons, and Jaws produced greater effects than eNpHR3.0 or ArchT ( Fig. 3e ; n = 8–32 units; P < 0.05, ANOVA with Newman-Keuls post hoc test).

span.label: photocurrents
span.quote: We subsequently engineered Halo57 by identifying K200R and W214F point mutations 19 , 20 ( Fig. 1b ), which significantly boosted photocurrents without altering its red action spectrum ( n = 9 or 10 cells; P = 0.02, ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc test), and by appending the KGC 21 or ER2 (ref. 22 ) trafficking sequences from the potassium channel Kir2.1 to result in the final molecules Jaws (KGC + ER2) and Jaws-ER2 (ER2)

span.label: rebound
span.quote: We similarly observed post-illumination rebound in Jaws-, eNpHR3.0- and ArchT-transduced neurons, and Jaws produced greater effects than eNpHR3.0 or ArchT ( Fig. 3e ; n = 8–32 units; P < 0.05, ANOVA with Newman-Keuls post hoc test).

span.label: point mutations
span.quote: We subsequently engineered Halo57 by identifying K200R and W214F point mutations 19 , 20 ( Fig. 1b ), which significantly boosted photocurrents without altering its red action spectrum ( n = 9 or 10 cells; P = 0.02, ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc test), and by appending the KGC 21 or ER2 (ref. 22 ) trafficking sequences from the potassium channel Kir2.1 to result in the final molecules Jaws (KGC + ER2) and Jaws-ER2 (ER2)

span.label: optogenetic inhibition here means a light-driven ION PUMP moving chloride inward, not a channel and not a synaptic silencer - the class matters because rebound and reversal behave differently
span.quote: Ion-specific solutions confirmed Jaws to be a light-driven chloride pump

span.label: noninvasive means no implanted optical device; the skull is intact but the virus was still injected surgically, and the paper's no-surgery scenario is explicitly future work with a transgenic line
span.quote: In principle, the need for brain surgery could be eliminated altogether by using transcranial illumination with a Jaws-expressing transgenic mouse strain

span.label: red-shifted is relative and small in absolute terms - a 14 nm shift from the standard halorhodopsin - and the practical gain comes from where that sits on the tissue absorption curve
span.quote: In vivo optogenetic inhibition has previously only been possible with blue, green and yellow light, as existing optogenetic inhibitors operate at only 10–30% of their peak capacity at red wavelengths.

span.label: percent inhibition here is computed over neurons SHOWING suppression, with unchanged and increased-firing units reported separately rather than folded in
span.quote: Using a similar strategy, we successfully inhibited neurons in the awake mouse cortex by delivering red light transcranially through the intact skull (635 nm, 10 mW/mm 2 out of a 1,500 µm fiber tip; Fig. 5a,b ) to regions 1–3 mm below the brain’s surface ( Fig. 5c,e,f ). Transcranial inhibition in the motor, somatosensory, insular and piriform cortices was efficient, with a 92 ± 14% decrease in firing for neurons showing suppression (mean ± s.d.; from 7 mice, n = 13 units; n = 9 units showed no change and n = 3 units showed an increase in activity

span.label: Jaws and Jaws-ER2 are two molecules differing in trafficking sequence and are reported separately throughout
span.quote: We subsequently engineered Halo57 by identifying K200R and W214F point mutations 19 , 20 ( Fig. 1b ), which significantly boosted photocurrents without altering its red action spectrum ( n = 9 or 10 cells; P = 0.02, ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc test), and by appending the KGC 21 or ER2 (ref. 22 ) trafficking sequences from the potassium channel Kir2.1 to result in the final molecules Jaws (KGC + ER2) and Jaws-ER2 (ER2)

span.label: builds-on → the authors' earlier identification of red-shifted cruxhalorhodopsins from H. marismortui and H. vallismortis (the paper's refs 1, 18)
span.quote: In earlier work, we identified two cruxhalorhodopsins from the haloarcula H. marismortui and H. vallismortis that possessed the most red-shifted action spectra known for any hyperpolarizing opsins 1 , 18 .

span.label: extends → previous halorhodopsin silencers (eNpHR, eNpHR3.0)
span.quote: Additionally, Jaws enabled significantly more inhibition of stimulus-evoked neural activity than possible with previous halorhodopsins.

span.label: replicates → previous reports of a minority of neurons increasing firing during optogenetic inhibition (the paper's refs 3, 40, 41)
span.quote: As others have reported, we observed a small number of neurons across multiple in vivo experiments that increased firing during optical illumination delivered either transcranially or from a 200-µm fiber, most likely as a result of network inhibition from upstream neurons 3 , 40 , 41 .

span.label: extends → earlier hyperpolarising pumps, which addressed about a cubic millimetre
span.quote: A major limit to the utility of optogenetic inhibition is the addressable quantity of neural tissue. Previous optogenetic hyperpolarizing proton pumps (Arch 1 , ArchT 3 , Mac 1 ) and chloride pumps (eNpHR 4 , eNpHR3.0 (ref. 2 )) have successfully inhibited volumes of approximately a cubic millimeter, but many neuroscience questions require the ability to suppress larger tissue volumes.

span.label: contradicts → the standing position that noninvasive optical inhibition was not achievable
span.quote: While a number of previous studies using channelrhodopsins have attempted to address this problem 11 – 16 , noninvasive optical inhibition has not yet been possible.

span.label: critiques → existing inhibitors' red-light performance, at 10-30% of peak capacity
span.quote: In vivo optogenetic inhibition has previously only been possible with blue, green and yellow light, as existing optogenetic inhibitors operate at only 10–30% of their peak capacity at red wavelengths.

span.label: extends → eNpHR-based cone reactivation in retinitis pigmentosa models, by widening the restored spike frequency range
span.quote: Jaws also enabled a broader peak spike frequency distribution than other opsins ( P < 0.05 for Jaws versus all other opsins, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test), with a mean frequency of 67.8 ± 7.0 Hz with eNpHR versus 189.5 ± 15.9 Hz with Jaws (values throughout are mean ± s.e.m. unless otherwise stated), increasing the spiking bandwidth by threefold

span.label: confirms → prior reports that a minority of neurons increase firing under optogenetic inhibition
span.quote: As others have reported, we observed a small number of neurons across multiple in vivo experiments that increased firing during optical illumination delivered either transcranially or from a 200-µm fiber, most likely as a result of network inhibition from upstream neurons

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · Jaws —is-a→ cruxhalorhodopsin
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span described a screen of the class without naming Jaws. This sentence names both IN APPOSITION - 'a red-shifted cruxhalorhodopsin, Jaws' - which is kind-membership stated as directly as a paper ever states it. — strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: We therefore screened members of the cruxhalorhodopsin class in primary neuronal culture to identify molecules with both red-shifted action spectra and robust photocurrents ( Fig. 1a and Supplementary Fig. 2 ) and identified a hyperpolarizer we named Halo57, the cruxhalorhodopsin from H. salinarum (strain Shark), with less than 60% homology to the Natronomonas pharaonis halorhodopsin

span.label: point mutations —causes→ photocurrents
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 1 — SIGN: increases, without moving the action spectrum - the two properties were separable
span.quote: We subsequently engineered Halo57 by identifying K200R and W214F point mutations 19 , 20 ( Fig. 1b ), which significantly boosted photocurrents without altering its red action spectrum ( n = 9 or 10 cells; P = 0.02, ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc test), and by appending the KGC 21 or ER2 (ref. 22 ) trafficking sequences from the potassium channel Kir2.1 to result in the final molecules Jaws (KGC + ER2) and Jaws-ER2 (ER2)

span.label: point mutations —distinct-from→ eNpHR3.0
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — CRITERION: the same two mutations do not help the halorhodopsin, so the gain belongs to this scaffold and not to the substitutions
span.quote: In accord with the low sequence conservation, the two homologous point mutations did not enhance the N. pharaonis halorhodopsin

span.label: hemoglobin —causes→ photocurrents
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — SIGN: limiting at short wavelengths - the absorption spectrum of blood is what sets the useful colour
span.quote: It has been previously well established that optical penetrance of mammalian tissues in the red to near-infrared (600–1,000 nm) wavelengths is better than that of bluer wavelengths, as a result of substantially less absorption from hemoglobin, myoglobin and lipid.

span.label: myelination —causes→ transcranial
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — SIGN: degrading, and preparation-specific - red penetrance is not a constant
span.quote: Despite this better red light penetrance, however, myelination may still affect optical propagation in neural tissue and should therefore be taken into account given the experimental system in question

span.label: Jaws —causes→ rebound
span.note: holds when: relative to eNpHR3.0 and ArchT - the comparison is between opsins, not against no opsin · direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — SIGN: worse than the tools it replaces. The paper reports the axis on which its own tool loses
span.quote: We similarly observed post-illumination rebound in Jaws-, eNpHR3.0- and ArchT-transduced neurons, and Jaws produced greater effects than eNpHR3.0 or ArchT ( Fig. 3e ; n = 8–32 units; P < 0.05, ANOVA with Newman-Keuls post hoc test).

span.label: tdTomato —distinct-from→ photocurrents
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — CRITERION: cells were chosen by a marker independent of opsin level, precisely so that the photocurrent comparison is not a comparison of expression
span.quote: To further characterize this, we transfected Jaws, eNpHR3.0 or ArchT into primary neuron cultures along with a secondary cytosolic tdTomato plasmid and selected cells for whole-cell patch clamp characterization solely on the basis of the presence of tdTomato ( Supplementary Fig. 4 ), to prevent selection bias for opsin expression levels and more accurately represent the full range of in vivo expression

span.label: apical dendrites —causes→ transcranial
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak — the confound that cannot be removed, because removing it would require illuminating deep tissue alone
span.quote: It is not possible to noninvasively illuminate only deep volumes with our experimental setup without also targeting surface and intermediate layers. We therefore cannot explicitly rule out the possibility that the observed noninvasive results were the result of indirect network activity or apical dendritic illumination: a caveat for any in vivo investigation of noninvasive optogenetics.

span.label: network inhibition —distinct-from→ rebound
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — two different reasons a neuron can fire more under an inhibitor; only one is a tool artefact
span.quote: As others have reported, we observed a small number of neurons across multiple in vivo experiments that increased firing during optical illumination delivered either transcranially or from a 200-µm fiber, most likely as a result of network inhibition from upstream neurons

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED FROM A NEITHER-ENDPOINT SPAN) · transcranial —contrasted-with→ optical fiber
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED FROM A NEITHER-ENDPOINT SPAN. The old span reported suppression over a distance range. This sentence sets the two delivery methods against each other by name - 'TRANSCRANIAL inhibition ... with a similar efficacy to standard invasive light delivery with a 200-um OPTICAL FIBER'. The contrast is between the methods; the similar efficacy is the finding ABOUT that contrast, not a denial of it. — strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: the fibre is the positive control, because its illumination is known to fall off within a few hundred microns
span.quote: Our paired recordings revealed similar degrees of suppression over a range of 1–3 mm below the brain’s surface ( Fig. 5i,j ). From this, we conclude Jaws is capable of noninvasive optogenetic inhibition comparable to the current standard of invasive optical delivery.

span.label: cone photoreceptors —causes→ retinal ganglion
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — the therapeutic logic: hyperpolarise the cone as light normally would, and the downstream cell spikes
span.quote: A potential therapy for patients with cone photoreceptor atrophy would be to resensitize the cone cells to light by genetically expressing light-activated hyperpolarizing ion pumps in the cone photoreceptors, which in their healthy state hyperpolarize in response to optical stimulation.

span.label: Jaws —is-a→ cruxhalorhodopsin
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — RE-GROUNDS Chuong2014-noninvasive-optical-inhibition-with-a-red-sh[0]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: We present a red-shifted cruxhalorhodopsin, Jaws, derived from Haloarcula ( Halobacterium ) salinarum (strain Shark) and engineered to result in red light–induced photocurrents three times those of earlier silencers.

span.label: transcranial —contrasted-with→ optical fiber
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — RE-GROUNDS Chuong2014-noninvasive-optical-inhibition-with-a-red-sh[9]: the old span named NEITHER endpoint.
span.quote: Jaws enabled efficacious transcranial inhibition of neural activity in awake mouse brain in response to red light, with a similar efficacy to standard invasive light delivery with a 200-µm optical fiber.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Two-sample comparisons were characterized with a two-tailed t -test, and multiway comparisons for a single variable were characterized with an ANOVA followed by a Newman-Keuls multiple comparison post-test between pairs.

span.label: ANOVA with Dunnett's post hoc test
span.term: ANOVA with Dunnett's post hoc test
span.quote: which significantly boosted photocurrents without altering its red action spectrum ( n = 9 or 10 cells; P = 0.02, ANOVA with Dunnett’s post hoc test)

span.label: paired t-test
span.quote: Paired tests were conducted with a two-tailed paired sample t -test.

span.label: Shapiro-Wilk normality test
span.quote: All data were tested for normality with a Shapiro-Wilk test.

span.label: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
span.quote: A Kolmogorov-Smirnov test was used to assess differences in spiking frequency distributions because of its sensitivity to both location and shape of cumulative distribution functions.

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: Briefly, spikes were detected and sorted offline using Offline Sorter (Plexon) or waveform template matching and principal component analysis discrimination

span.label: ANOVA with Newman-Keuls post hoc test
span.term: ANOVA with Newman-Keuls post hoc test
span.quote: we found Jaws to have significantly higher red light (632 nm) photocurrents than eNpHR3.0 or ArchT across all tested light powers ( Fig. 1f and Supplementary Fig. 4d ; n = 21–30 cells from 2 batches of culture; P < 0.01 for 0.1–20 mW/mm 2 , ANOVA with Newman-Keuls post hoc test).

span.label: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
span.quote: Jaws also enabled a broader peak spike frequency distribution than other opsins ( P < 0.05 for Jaws versus all other opsins, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test), with a mean frequency of 67.8 ± 7.0 Hz with eNpHR versus 189.5 ± 15.9 Hz with Jaws (values throughout are mean ± s.e.m. unless otherwise stated), increasing the spiking bandwidth by threefold

span.label: Jaws produced significantly larger red-light photocurrents than the existing silencers eNpHR3.0 and ArchT at every light power tested in cultured neurons.
span.quote: we found Jaws to have significantly higher red light (632 nm) photocurrents than eNpHR3.0 or ArchT across all tested light powers

span.label: Jaws strongly suppressed visually evoked cortical activity in vivo and restored light-driven retinal ganglion spiking in retinitis pigmentosa model mice.
span.quote: Jaws exhibits robust inhibition of sensory-evoked neural activity in the cortex and results in strong light responses when used in retinas of retinitis pigmentosa model mice.

span.label: Red light delivered through the intact skull silenced neurons millimetres deep in awake mice, making optogenetic inhibition noninvasive.
span.quote: We also demonstrate that Jaws can noninvasively mediate transcranial optical inhibition of neurons deep in the brains of awake mice.

span.label: Transcranial red-light illumination cut firing by roughly 92% in suppressed units across motor, somatosensory, insular and piriform cortex.
span.quote: Transcranial inhibition in the motor, somatosensory, insular and piriform cortices was efficient, with a 92 ± 14% decrease in firing for neurons showing suppression

span.label: Gradually ramping the light off more than halved the post-illumination rebound firing rate, showing that pulse shaping can mitigate rebound.
span.quote: We attempted to ameliorate this by gradually ramping down illumination over a duration of 200–1,000 ms and found that the mean rebound instantaneous firing rate dropped significantly, from 52 ± 12 Hz to 23 ± 6 Hz ( n = 16 units; P = 0.0065, paired t -test), suggesting that sculpting of light pulses may enable rebound reduction.

span.label: Jaws gave significantly larger red-light photocurrents than eNpHR3.0 or ArchT at every power tested
span.quote: we found Jaws to have significantly higher red light (632 nm) photocurrents than eNpHR3.0 or ArchT across all tested light powers ( Fig. 1f and Supplementary Fig. 4d ; n = 21–30 cells from 2 batches of culture; P < 0.01 for 0.1–20 mW/mm 2 , ANOVA with Newman-Keuls post hoc test).

span.label: visually evoked cortical activity fell by about 86% under yellow light in Jaws-expressing cortex
span.quote: Inhibition of visually evoked neural activity was strong ( Fig. 3a,b ), with an 86 ± 3% reduction of visually evoked activity in Jaws-expressing cortex ( Fig. 3c ; from 4 mice, n = 27 units with a significant reduction in firing; n = 3 units showed no change and n = 3 units showed a significant increase in firing) over a range of evoked firing rates (1.8–12.5 Hz; Supplementary Fig. 6a ), and consistent across a range of input contrast strengths

span.label: under red light Jaws inhibited about 89-97% while eNpHR3.0 fell to 27.5%, against 76% at its own yellow peak
span.quote: As expected, both Jaws variants robustly inhibited spontaneous neural activity when illuminated with either red (88.8 ± 15.9% inhibition for Jaws, 97.2 ± 3.9% inhibition for Jaws-ER2) or yellow wavelengths (94.2 ± 9.3% inhibition for Jaws, 99.0 ± 1.6% inhibition for Jaws-ER2), while eNpHR3.0’s red-light inhibition dropped significantly to only 27.5 ± 30.3% relative to its peak yellow-light performance of 76.1 ± 11.1% inhibition ( Fig. 4f ; n = 5 or 6 units, P = 0.0121)

span.label: transcranial illumination through intact skull suppressed firing by about 92% in neurons showing suppression, 1-3 mm deep
span.quote: Using a similar strategy, we successfully inhibited neurons in the awake mouse cortex by delivering red light transcranially through the intact skull (635 nm, 10 mW/mm 2 out of a 1,500 µm fiber tip; Fig. 5a,b ) to regions 1–3 mm below the brain’s surface ( Fig. 5c,e,f ). Transcranial inhibition in the motor, somatosensory, insular and piriform cortices was efficient, with a 92 ± 14% decrease in firing for neurons showing suppression (mean ± s.d.; from 7 mice, n = 13 units; n = 9 units showed no change and n = 3 units showed an increase in activity

span.label: transdural illumination suppressed firing by about 86% in medial prefrontal cortex
span.quote: Using red illumination ( Fig. 5a ), we found we could transdurally inhibit neurons in the medial prefrontal cortex of a mouse, with a 86 ± 13% decrease (mean ± s.d.) in firing for neurons showing suppression ( n = 66 units across 2 anesthetized mice
